title: Pylon vs Intercom in 2026: which fits B2B support?
summary: Choose Intercom (now Fin) if most of your support starts in your product's chat.
body_markdown:
Choose Pylon if your customers are companies that reach you in shared Slack or Teams channels and need account-level context and SLAs. In Pylon, agents investigate issues before your team opens them, using the customer's account context. Choose Intercom (now Fin) if most of your support starts in your product's chat. Intercom's Fin AI Agent is billed per outcome and can run on other help desks. Pylon is priced per seat plus agentic credits, with no per-issue fees. Intercom renamed itself Fin in May 2026, and Salesforce completed its acquisition of Fin in September 2026.


## How do Pylon and Intercom compare?


Pylon Intercom


Built for B2B support organized by customer account Customer service with in-app messaging and Fin


Agents Support Agent, Assist Agent, Slack Agent, Automations, and Skills Fin AI Agent. Copilot is an add-on, billed per agent.


AI pricing Agentic credits shared across the team. No per-issue fees. Fin billed per outcome


Seat pricing Professional $89 per seat per month and Advanced $139 per seat per month, on an annual contract Essential $29, Advanced $85, Expert $132 per seat per month, billed annually, plus $0.99 per Fin outcome.


Slack Connect Native channel on every plan Supports customers in Slack


Microsoft Teams Advanced and above Fin answers in Microsoft Teams channels, and those conversations appear in the Intercom inbox


MCP server Read and write on every plan. Sends customer replies and posts internal notes. Reads data, creates and updates articles, and adds internal notes. Can't send customer-facing replies.


Help center Included, with AI article generation Public help center on the base plan


Security SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, GDPR, and EU data residency on every plan. HIPAA on Advanced and above. HIPAA on its top plan


AI on another help desk Pylon is the full help desk Fin can run on other help desks


## When does Intercom fit better?


- Most conversations start in your web or mobile app.
- You want an AI agent on top of the help desk you already have.
- You mostly support individual users one to one.


## When does Pylon fit better?


- Your customers are companies with many users, contracts, and SLAs.
- Customers expect support in shared Slack Connect or Teams channels.
- Your team often hands issues to engineering through Jira, Linear, GitHub Issues, Asana, or Shortcut.
- You want Pylon's agents and your own AI tools, through MCP, working from the same account data.


## What happened when teams moved from Intercom to Pylon?


- **Loop** moved in one month without disruption. Average resolution time fell 20%, and about 25% of customers are now supported in Slack.
- **Lightdash** brought Slack Connect, Slack Community, email, and in-app chat into one place, and replaced Intercom for in-app chat.


Owen Murk, Product Support Specialist at Loop: "Our responsibilities differ a lot across people and accounts. Intercom worked for agents who just answer a ticket and move to the next one, but that was a really small percentage of the support we were doing."


## How long does a switch from Intercom take?


Loop finished in one month. Your timeline depends on data volume, workflows, and channels.


## FAQ


### Is Pylon an Intercom alternative?


Yes, for B2B teams. Pylon is a full help desk for account-based support across Slack, Teams, email, and chat.


### Does Intercom have an MCP server?


Yes. It reads conversations, contacts, companies, and articles, creates and updates articles, and adds internal notes. It can't send customer-facing replies. Pylon's MCP server can send customer replies and post internal notes.


### Does Pylon have an MCP server?


Yes. It reads and writes, it's on every plan, and it works from Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor.


### How does pricing differ?


Pylon Professional is $89 per seat per month and Advanced is $139 per seat per month, on an annual contract. Agentic features run on credits, and there are no per-issue fees. Intercom charges per seat, plus a per-outcome fee for Fin.


### Is Intercom now part of Salesforce?


Yes. Salesforce completed its acquisition of Fin, formerly Intercom, on September 10, 2026. Fin operates within Salesforce AI Labs, and the Intercom help desk product keeps its name.
